scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01, requested by SH-CS).
symptoms: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1200/month between Jun-Jul and Aug-Sep (E-02).
Field manual-read route completion fell to 88% vs a 95% target across 9,200 accounts since August (E-01).
59% of disputed bills carry an ACTUAL (non-estimated) read type rather than ESTIMATED (E-04).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1200/month (Aug-Sep) (E-02), driven by a rise in incorrect bills rather than slow ticket handling, since response times remain within SLA (E-03) and no tariff change occurred (E-07). The best-supported, uncontradicted mechanism is a billing import/validation defect since August that is misbilling both estimate-substituted reads and bills carrying ACTUAL reads (H-RULE-CHANGE-MISBILLING, supported by E-04, 59% of disputed bills are ACTUAL-read), compounded by field manual-read route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 accounts since August (E-01).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-04 revised by E-11: The observed split (1,240 ESTIMATED / 1,785 ACTUAL of 3,025 disputed bills) still stands, but per E-11 the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read bills are 100% AMI-channel reads rejected at import, not manual-read outcomes, so E-04 no longer supports linking the ESTIMATED share to the field-route-completion mechanism in PR-CHAIN-1/PR-ROOT.

F-03.statement: CRM dispute response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling capacity/response-speed problem that an AI auto-answering agent would resolve, rather than an underlying billing-accuracy defect.

H-RULE-CHANGE-MISBILLING.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) around August caused reads to be mis-validated or rejected, producing estimated/incorrect bills that drove the dispute surge.

H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery from the vendor (ORG-AMI) degraded or failed starting August, forcing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter reading (ORG-FIELD) degraded (missed routes, staffing) since August, increasing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-TICKET-REPORTING-ARTIFACT.statement: The apparent doubling of dispute tickets is partly a CRM categorization/reporting artifact rather than a real doubling of incorrect bills.

H-TARIFF-OR-IMPORT-ERROR-ACTUA.statement: Bills built from ACTUAL reads are themselves being mis-billed (e.g., tariff application or import-validation defect) during Aug-Sep, independent of read availability.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for the Aug-Sep dispute-surge period was 88% against a 95% target, with 9,200 accounts on manual-read routes — a measurable shortfall in manual meter reading coverage during the exact window the dispute surge occurred.

The observed 88% route completion against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts still stands as a genuine field-operations shortfall, but it no longer explains or is 'compounded by' the ESTIMATED-read dispute symptom, since E-11 shows that disputed ESTIMATED population is 100% AMI-channel, not on manual-read routes.

CRM dispute volume rose from ~600/month in Jun-Jul (610, 590) to ~1200/month in Aug-Sep (1180, 1260), confirming a real roughly 2x rise in ticket counts coincident with the period cited in E-01. This quantifies the magnitude of the surge CL-01 claims but does not by itself indicate its underlying cause.

CRM response-time data (2440 tickets) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA, indicating ticket response speed is already within target and is not the bottleneck behind the dispute surge.

Of 3,025 disputed bills, 1,240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read type and 1,785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read type — the majority of disputes are tied to bills that had a normal, non-estimated read, not to estimate substitution.

The observed split (1,240 ESTIMATED / 1,785 ACTUAL of 3,025 disputed bills) still stands, but per E-11 the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read bills are 100% AMI-channel reads rejected at import, not manual-read outcomes, so E-04 no longer supports linking the ESTIMATED share to the field-route-completion mechanism in PR-CHAIN-1/PR-ROOT.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year. This is an unverified stakeholder statement, not an authoritative tool record, so it only weakens the tariff-application portion of H-TARIFF-OR-IMPORT-ERROR-ACTUA pending confirmation via tariff_change_log.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortfall of three meter readers since July has caused manual-read routes to run late, resulting in estimated bills for the affected customers. This is an unverified stakeholder claim offering a candidate causal mechanism consistent with H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION, but it does not quantify scope and does not address why E-04 shows most disputed bills carry ACTUAL (not ESTIMATED) reads.

SH-FIELD's unverified claim that late manual routes cause estimated bills for affected customers still stands as a stakeholder claim about manual-read accounts, but it no longer applies to the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, since E-11 shows that population is AMI-channel and traces to billing-import rejection, not manual-read lateness.

The authoritative billing-db tariff_change_log returned zero records, confirming no tariff change occurred this year; this agrees with and authoritatively settles what E-05/CL-02 had only claimed informally.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract document (E-08) confirms the authorization pathway for push_route_update: the utility may request route priority changes but execution requires Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation, consistent with the already-recorded K-DISPATCH constraint. It bears on the authorization/process question, not on the causal hypotheses for the dispute surge.

This is the account/route-level linkage needed to cross-reference against route-log's lagging routes, but by itself it does not yet establish how many of these 320 accounts fall on routes affected by the field-reader shortage, nor how they relate to the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills in E-04.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor-side) reports MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), per E-10. This is an unverified stakeholder claim about tooling/access status, not actual AMI read event data, so it does not by itself confirm or deny any read-delivery or misbilling mechanism; its main effect is that the previously access-pending mdms-export query may now be retried.

Now that MDMS export access is available, authoritative AMI read-event data for the disputed ESTIMATED-read population (1,184+56=1,240, matching E-04's ESTIMATED count exactly) shows 95% (1,184) had an AMI read delivered before cutoff and exported to billing but REJECTED at import for "high consumption," while only 56 (4.5%) truly had no read received. This means almost all ESTIMATED-read disputed bills trace to a billing-import validation rejection on valid AMI reads, not to AMI delivery failure or to manual field-read lateness (these are AMI-channel events, not manual-read accounts).

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.question: Did a billing import validation rule change actually occur around August, and what specifically changed to cause ACTUAL-read bills to be misbilled?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.decision_impact: Confirms or disconfirms the core premise hypothesis H-RULE-CHANGE-MISBILLING that the whole root_problem rests on; without it, any downstream fix target is unverified.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule-change log (DA-RULES) for changes effective around August and cross-reference the changed rule ids against the disputed ACTUAL-read bill ids in billing-db.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.safe_placeholder: Proceed only with read-only diagnostic cross-referencing; withhold any billing-fix recommendation to Billing Operations until the rule-change log confirms the specific defect.

U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SCOPE.question: What share of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills is attributable to the field route completion shortfall versus other causes?
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SCOPE.decision_impact: Determines whether and how much route-dispatch remediation (push_route_update) is warranted versus other causes of the ESTIMATED-read dispute share.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SCOPE.resolution_path: Join route-log completion records with the CRM disputed-account list by account id to quantify the overlap between late/incomplete routes and ESTIMATED-read disputes.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SCOPE.safe_placeholder: Treat the field shortfall as a contributing, not sole, cause and do not request any route priority change until the overlap is quantified.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SCOPE.resolution: E-11 shows the full 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed-bill population is tied to AMI-channel read events (not manual-read accounts), implying the field route completion shortfall explains little to none of this population and the dominant cause is the import-validation rejection.

U-AMI-DATA-AVAILABILITY.question: Once vendor-provisioned MDMS export access is available, does AMI read data show delivery issues relevant to the disputed ACTUAL-read bills, despite H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE being contradicted by current evidence?
U-AMI-DATA-AVAILABILITY.decision_impact: Could reopen the AMI-delivery hypothesis for the ACTUAL-read portion of disputes if vendor data later shows gaps not visible from billing-db alone.
U-AMI-DATA-AVAILABILITY.resolution_path: Await vendor-provisioned mdms-export access (currently blocked, ACCESS_PENDING per recovery log) then query read_events_for_disputed_estimated.
U-AMI-DATA-AVAILABILITY.safe_placeholder: Proceed with the billing-config rule-change investigation independently of AMI data; keep H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE closed as REJECTED pending that data.
U-AMI-DATA-AVAILABILITY.resolution: With MDMS export access now available, AMI read data (E-11) shows no major delivery failure (only 56/1240 undelivered); the dominant pattern is valid AMI reads rejected at billing import for high consumption, keeping H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE rejected and pointing to an import-validation mechanism.

U-TICKET-VOLUME-MEASUREMENT-VA.question: Does any part of the ticket-count doubling reflect a CRM categorization/tagging change rather than a real increase in incorrect bills?
U-TICKET-VOLUME-MEASUREMENT-VA.decision_impact: Affects whether M-DISPUTE-TICKETS-MONTHLY is a valid success measure or needs normalization before being used as the baseline-recovery target.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-MEASUREMENT-VA.resolution_path: Audit CRM ticket categorization/tagging rule changes since July to determine if any part of the volume increase is a measurement artifact.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-MEASUREMENT-VA.safe_placeholder: Report monthly dispute volume with a measurement-validity caveat until the categorization audit is complete; do not treat raw count alone as fully dispositive.

U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF.question: Is the daily manual-read upload handoff (H-FIELD-BILL, ORG-FIELD to ORG-UTIL) delivering complete and semantically valid reads, or could handoff failures be contributing to the ESTIMATED/ACTUAL misbilling split?
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF.decision_impact: If the handoff itself is dropping or corrupting reads, the route-completion and rule-change diagnostics would be analyzing an incomplete picture of the input data.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF.resolution_path: Verify H-FIELD-BILL delivery completeness and semantic validity by reconciling daily upload record counts against route-log completed routes and billing-db import records.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF.safe_placeholder: Treat field-route-based shortfall attribution as provisional and flag it as such until the handoff's delivery/semantic validity is confirmed.
